newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - June 30.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - June 30.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends ***********************************************
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:
CANNES - Two ads for Diesel jeans created by the Swedish advertising agency Paradist DDB Stockholm won the top prize at the annual International Advertising Festival.

NEW YORK - A California court has ordered a temporary halt to a marketing programme launched by brewer Anheuser-Busch. The promotion offers beer mugs, pool tables and other merchandise to consumers who drink Budweiser beer and accumulate redeemable "Bud" points but the state contends the program violates state regulations.

CANNES - China is expected to become the world's fourth largest advertising market in the next five years and Western-based ad agencies foresee no problems with the Hong Kong handover, the head of Ogilvy & Mather's Asia-Pacific region says.

CANNES - Martin Sorrell, chairman of WPP Group Plc, criticises advertising agencies for losing media-planning and media-buying business. He says media buyers such as Carat and CIA are growing at the expense of ad agencies.

CANNES - Advertisers and ad agencies are making increasing efforts to reach consumers worldwide by tapping into local tastes and cultures, and are learning how difficult it is to market a product globaly with a single ad campaign, executives tell Reuters at Cannes festival.
LONDON - DDB International establishes presence in Tunisia by joining forces with Ceres Conseil, the leading communications group in Tunisia, with an ad agency and printing and publication divisions.

CANNES - Creative teams in French advertising agencies lack inspiration at present because of France's economic crisis, says Jacques Seguela,vice-chairman of Havas Advertising and a French advertising industry guru.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

WASHINGTON - The Clinton administration, after a two-year study, has decided not to call for new taxes or regulations on business conducted over the Internet, The Washington Post reports. The administration will let the private sector largely determine how it will operate in cyberspace, the newspaper says.

PARIS - French pay television group Canal Plus is preparing to leave the German pay television market altogether and focus on European countries that hold more promise for it, like Italy, company executives tell the Canal Plus annual meeting.
LONDON United News & Media Plc takes control of more than 50 percent of HTV Group Plc after launching an agreed 371.7 million pound ($617.9 million) bid for the regional broadcaster.

SYDNEY - Australian pay television operator Foxtel says it will increase the cost of its basic package and increase the number of channels it offers. Foxtel is owned by News Corp Ltd and the Australian government's Telstra Corp.
PARIS - Pierre Dauzier, chairman of French media group Havas, says the Havas board will not look at proposals to divest weekly news magazines Le Point and L'Express until September.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

WASHINGTON - President Bill Clinton plans to propose raising cigarette taxes by 20 cents per pack, with revenues generated to be placed in a trust fund for children's healthcare, public health and other programmes, a White House official says.

NEW YORK - PepsiCo Inc intends to ends it agreement next year to distribute Ocean Spray drinks, the Wall Street Journal says. The paper says the move may signal PepsiCo's desire to develop and market its own line of juice drinks.
STOCKHOLM - Swedish vehicle maker AB Volvo says it can succeed without merging with any other company, although cooperation with Japan's Mitsubishi should continue.

LONDON - UK's Whitbread Plc will crack down on the sale of co-called "alcopops" to under-age drinkers, the Financial Times says. Whitbread, one of the biggest manufacturers of the sweet alcoholic drinks, has been in touch with the Home Office suggesting a series of measures to curb teenage drinking, the newspaper reports.
MANILA - Philippine food and beverage giant San Miguel Corp says it is reducing the prices of its beer, in a major move to boost sales and reverse slowing demand.
TOKYO - Toshiba, Japan's top personal computer maker, announces plans to boost production in order to grab a larger share of the booming worldwide computer market.

MANILA - General Motors Corp says it is still interested in pursuing talks with the Philippines even through local officials say they are not keen on relaxing investment rules to accommodate the U.S. car giant.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

CHICAGO - The answer to the age-old question -- "What's for dinner?" -- is going to get a lot more complicated in the United States. Mid-life Baby Boomers will be demanding more variety in their diets in the future, from exotic Asian and African cuisines to down-home staples like mashed potatoes and meatloaf, says Faith Popcorn, chairman of New York-based BrainReserve Inc, which predicts consumer trends.

LONDON- Car mania in Asia and Latin America threatens to wipe out any gains made in protecting the world from automobile pollution. Most new petrol-powered cars no longer pump out killer gases, but this progress is threatened by an explosion of car ownership over the next 10 years in new markets, say industry experts.

WASAGA BEACH, Ontario - Canada's first topless shop opens in this popular Ontario resort. Crowds of gaping onlookers gathered as customers -- both women and men -- agree to shop topless to promote the opening of Tom & Tina's Topless Surf & Sport, clothing store. "It's a free-spirited store," says shop owner David Blackstone.
NEW DELHI - India is hoping to boost the number of tourists visiting the country to five million by the year 2000 from 2.3 million visitors this year, says the minister of tourism.

OSLO - Two Norwegian designers believe they have the solution to traffic congestion and related pollution -- the first ever combined solar and wind-power vehicle. The pair say their car is based on a principle similar to the motorised rickshaw popular in many of the world's most over-populated cities.
